To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrical conductivity of PT was increased by doping with metal ions, which was due to an increase in the charge mobility of the composites.
the conductivity of PT was enhanced by doping with copper(II) ions and the conductivity mechanism was found to be different from that of PT.
the charge transport mechanism in the composites of PT and copper(II) acetate is different from that of pure PT and that there are two frequency-dependent conductivity regions in the composites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new materials with a view to understanding their electrical properties.
the study of the influence of the addition of copper acetylacetonato to the electrical properties of a polythiophenes.
the synthesis of new materials, which can be used in the development of organic electronics, and in particular organic light‐emitting diodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of Cu(acac) 2 to PT matrix has led to a significant increase in conductivity of PT matrix composites.
the addition of metal ion into polymer matrix affects its thermal stability and conductivity.
there is a strong evidence that copper(II) ions have been adsorbed onto PT chains, and the adsorption process is an electrostatic one, as shown in Fig. 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully prepared PT/Cu(acac) 2 composite samples and characterized them via different techniques.
the electrical conductivity of PT was improved by the incorporation of Cu(II) ions.
the conductivity of the composites is controlled by the charge transport mechanism and that this is affected by the doping process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charge transport mechanism in PT composites is different from that of PT and that the charge transport in the composites is controlled by both grain boundaries and the bulk material.
the charge transport mechanism in PT/Cu(acac) composites is different from that reported in literature for PT/Cu(ac) composites.
the conductivity of the composites is strongly affected by the doping process, which in turn is affected by the concentration of the metal salt.
